To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) count-min sketches are an efficient and privacy-preserving way for exporting a (part) of a KB towards a receiving party, (ii) the privacy level of a count-min sketch can be tuned by setting its collision probability, and (iii) the accuracy of computations performed on an exported KB can be affected by the privacy level of the sketch

1) count-min sketch is a suitable data structure to export data in privacy-preserving fashion; 2) count-min sketch can be tuned to preserve privacy; 3) noise can be added in count-min sketches to ensure controlled error; 4) the tradeoff between computation accuracy and privacy preservation can be controlled.

\begin{enumerate} \item Count-min sketches can achieve privacy in KBs export; \item The accuracy of a computation is inversely correlated with privacy; \item The γ-deniability can be used to tune the privacy level of a count-min sketch; \item The addition of noise to a count-min sketches can be used to protect the exported KB from linkage attacks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of enabling a party to export a part of its KB towards a receiving one, while preserving its privacy and controlling the accuracy of the exported KB.
the problem of enabling parties to export their KBs towards a receiving one, in a privacy-preserved way.

the following questions: \emph{How can a count-min sketch be used for privacy-preserving KB export? How can the privacy level be measured in terms of deniablity? What is the impact of privacy preservation on the accuracy of the computation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the count-min sketch data structure can provide a good tradeoff between privacy and computation accuracy, and can be a good solution to enable privacy-preserving KB sharing.

the privacy-preserving KB export based on the count-min sketch enables parties to share data in a privacy preserving way, and to achieve a given privacy level, while still preserving the accuracy of computations performed on exported data.
count-min sketch-based privacy-preserving KB sharing is feasible, but it requires a good tradeoff between privacy and accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel approach to export data in the context of knowledge bases that enables privacy-preserving data exchange between parties.
count-min sketches can be used to export data in privacy-preserving fashion with a tunable privacy level, but with a certain accuracy cost.
count-min sketches can be used to export a KB in a privacy-presering manner, while maintaining a good accuracy for a given privacy level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
count-min sketches enable to export KB data while preserving privacy.
, in the presence of a privacy requirement, a party can share its data with another one without disclosing any sensitive information.
the count-min sketch is a powerful tool for privacy-preserving knowledge base sharing, and that the privacy level can be tuned to obtain different levels of privacy preservation.
